title: August and the Spire
premise: Marguerite Quintana carves charms from bone and hears the dead whisper through them, a gift the valley of Hollowmere was founded to shield from magic's reach. When the usurper King Aldric declares a realm-wide hunt for the gifted, his inquisitors breach the valley, killing her mentor and dragging Marguerite toward the capital as bait for other survivors. Alongside a defected inquisitor, Tomas, and the ghost of a queen murdered by Aldric, she learns the valley's peace depends on an ancient covenant between the living and the dead — one Aldric broke to seize power. To end the hunt, Marguerite must carry the covenant's shattered keystone to the Spire at the world's edge, reforge it by surrendering her own memories as payment, and choose which parts of herself survive. She succeeds, but forgets Tomas entirely; he stays beside her anyway, and the dead finally rest.
about_author: Lior Winterbourne is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing funeral customs across three continents before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about grief, memory, and the bargains people make to keep going.

chapters.title: The Quiet Valley
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. We meet Hollowmere, where magic cannot follow, and watch Marguerite carve a bone charm that lets a widow speak once more to her dead husband. The beat is warmth shadowed by loneliness: Marguerite serves the grieving but has never been allowed to grieve openly herself.

chapters.title: Whispers in the Marrow
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A charm cracks mid-ritual and the dead inside it scream a warning: riders are coming, wearing no colors she knows. Her mentor, Odile, goes pale and begins burning papers. The emotional beat is dread arriving gently, like weather, before the storm.

chapters.title: Riders in Grey
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV introduces him as an inquisitor leading the hunt into Hollowmere, ordered to take 'the bone-carver' alive. He watches his men torch a shrine and feels the first hairline fracture in his loyalty. The beat is complicity — evil seen from inside its uniform.

chapters.title: What Odile Knew
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Inquisitors seize Odile; before they do, she presses a shard of pale stone into Marguerite's hand — a piece of the covenant keystone — and tells her to run north. Odile dies refusing to name her student. The beat is loss and inheritance in a single breath.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She doesn't run fast enough; captured, she is marched out of the valley, feeling magic flood back into the world around her like pressure on old wounds. The dead grow louder outside Hollowmere. The beat is disorientation — leaving home as a prisoner, not a pilgrim.

chapters.title: The Queen Who Wouldn't Rest
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, in a prison wagon. The keystone shard lets her hear Queen Isolde, murdered by Aldric, whose spirit clings to it. Isolde reveals the covenant between living and dead was broken to fuel Aldric's armies. The beat is reluctant alliance with a ghost who despises being pitied.

chapters.title: An Inquisitor's Doubt
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Interrogating a gifted child, Tomas falsifies his report to spare her, and realizes Aldric's hunt feeds something darker than policy. He requests transfer to guard the bone-carver. The beat is a man choosing to stop looking away.

chapters.title: The Gilded Cage
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Marguerite arrives in the capital, displayed as proof the hunt works; Tomas becomes her jailer. Their wary conversations over chess reveal each is lying about what they believe. The beat is two guarded people circling the same truth.

chapters.title: Aldric's Bargain
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. We learn he broke the covenant deliberately: the dead's unrest powers his war-machines and his immortality, but it is consuming him — he no longer remembers his daughter's face. The beat is horror at power that devours its holder from within.

chapters.title: Escape Through the Bone Market
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. With Isolde's guidance and Tomas's deliberate negligence, Marguerite flees during the Bone Market festival, stealing back confiscated charms. Tomas burns his own commission behind them. The beat is exhilaration laced with guilt — freedom bought with betrayal.

chapters.title: Road of Small Ghosts
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Fleeing north toward the free cities, the trio passes villages hollowed by conscription, where Marguerite frees restless dead from unmarked graves. Tomas confronts what his orders built. The beat is reckoning made physical, mile by mile.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Close Their Gates
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The free cities refuse refugees, fearing Aldric's retaliation; a council elder demands proof the covenant can be reforged before offering aid. Marguerite, exhausted, nearly gives up. The beat is despair — survival means nothing if everyone locks their doors.

chapters.title: Isolde's Confession
chapters.summary: Isolde's ghost narrates her murder and her own complicity: she signed the covenant's original terms knowing the price would fall on the voiceless. The beat is moral complexity — even the sympathetic dead owe debts.

chapters.title: The Hunt Closes
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. His general, Veyra, tracks the keystone shard and razes a waystation, killing allies Marguerite had made. Aldric feels each death as nourishment and hates himself less each time. The beat is corruption completing its circuit.

chapters.title: What the Dead Ask
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At a covenant shrine, the assembled dead tell her the keystone can only be reforged at the Spire, and the price is memory given willingly — every recollection surrendered feeding the bond. She must choose what to pay. The beat is terror of self-erasure.

chapters.title: Veyra at the Ford
chapters.summary: Action chapter, shared POV. Veyra's army corners them at a river crossing; free-city volunteers arrive, having been moved by freed ghosts' testimony. Tomas takes a wound shielding Marguerite. The beat is costly solidarity — others now bleed for her cause.

chapters.title: The Ascent
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Wounded and hunted, they climb toward the Spire through a pass where the veil is thin and Marguerite walks briefly among all her own dead, including Odile, who forgives her. The beat is grace granted before the final price.

chapters.title: The Spire
chapters.summary: Climax part one. At the Spire's summit, Aldric confronts them, offering Marguerite her memories' safety in exchange for serving him. Isolde manifests fully and unmakes his borrowed years while Tomas holds off Veyra. The beat is temptation answered with sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Climax part two. Marguerite feeds her memories into the keystone — her mother's face, her valley, Tomas — and seals the covenant, returning the dead to rest and stripping Aldric's power. He crumbles into an ordinary, dying man. The beat is transcendence through loss.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Stranger
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Marguerite wakes remembering nothing of him or her past; Isolde, fading, leaves one last gift — a carved bone bead holding a single memory Marguerite may open or not. The beat is tenderness without ownership.

chapters.title: The Valley Remembers
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The free cities shelter the gifted; Hollowmere reopens its borders. Marguerite rebuilds her workshop, hearing silence where the dead used to press — and finding it peaceful rather than empty. The beat is quiet restoration.

chapters.title: August and the Spire
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Marguerite's POV. On an August evening, she opens the bead and chooses to remember only one thing: not Tomas's name, but the feeling of being trusted. He sits across from her anyway, beginning again. The beat is hope — love that survives being forgotten.
